title: An 8-Billion-Agent Earth Simulation, and Google's AI Brain Drain Meets Cloud's Best Quarter
tldr: Harvard and MIT researchers built MatrAIx, an 8.3-billion-agent LLM simulation of Earth's population — worth watching for large-scale behavior/market simulation.
SemiAnalysis called Gemini 'cooked' after six senior AI leaders left Google (including self-described 'LLM inventor' Noam Shazeer) — yet Google Cloud still grew 82% YoY to $24B.
Claude Tag now lets you delegate real work to @Claude inside Slack — steps and a ready-to-use prompt included.

tips.heading: Delegate real work to Claude directly in Slack
steps: Open Claude Tag, click "Add to Slack," and complete setup.
Grant it access to the channels where you want help, then type @Claude plus your task with enough context — treat it like a coworker, not a chatbot.
Keep working while Claude researches, drafts, summarizes, or completes the task.
Review the response, edit as needed, and use the output.
tips.prompt: @Claude Review the last week's product discussion in this channel. Summarize the key decisions, list any open action items, identify blockers, and draft a Slack update I can share with leadership.

tips.heading: Make AI writing clearer by naming the rules you want
steps: When output reads stiff or bloated, tell your AI to write in Simplified Technical English, or to follow Zinsser's four principles of quality writing (clarity, simplicity, brevity, humanity).
Ask it to revise the same passage against those rules rather than starting over from scratch.
Save the instruction as a standing rule for reports, proposals, or client emails.

tips.heading: Break out of generic AI output with an anti-pattern step
steps: First ask your LLM to generate "the most stereotypical" version of what you want — a design, an email, a plan.
Use that output as a list of clichés to avoid.
Ask for a new version that deliberately departs from those patterns.

news.body: Harvard and MIT researchers built MatrAIx, an AI simulation of Earth's population using 8.3 billion LLM agents modeled on real human profiles pulled from public records and supplemented with synthetic personas, built by a 200-plus-scientist team.
news.means: A preview of large-scale agent simulation as a research and market-testing tool — worth watching if a client ever asks about simulating customer or population behavior at scale instead of running real panels.

news.body: SemiAnalysis declared Gemini "cooked" after a wave of senior departures — Jeff Dean, Sanjay Ghemawat, Quoc Le, Oriol Vinyals, Noam Shazeer, and John Jumper have all left Google, reportedly slowed by internal bureaucracy that has Gemini 3.5 Pro running months behind schedule. Despite the exodus, Google Cloud revenue hit $24B last quarter, up 82% year-over-year — roughly double AWS's and Azure's growth rates.
news.means: A vendor-stability data point worth flagging before recommending Gemini for a client build — the infrastructure business is thriving even as the model team churns.
